knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 39-year-old male patient with no significant past medical history presented with blurry vision in the left eye. He reported no history of travel or recent sick contacts. He works as a welder and does not always use protective gear. The ophthalmic exam revealed panuveitis of the left eye. He complained of blurry vision in his left eye; however, he denied any chest pain, shortness of breath, hemoptysis, night sweats, or fevers. His physical exam was unremarkable.. Confirmed diagnosis: Ocular Tuberculosis. Differential diagnosis includes: Ocular Tuberculosis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Ocular Tuberculosis

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 39-year-old male patient with no significant past medical history presented with blurry vision in the left eye. He reported no history of travel or recent sick contacts. He works as a welder and does not always use protective gear. The ophthalmic exam revealed panuveitis of the left eye. He complained of blurry vision in his left eye; however, he denied any chest pain, shortness of breath, hemoptysis, night sweats, or fevers. His physical exam was unremarkable. Labs were significant for a positive QuantiFERON. Chest X-ray was negative for infiltrates, cavities, or lymphadenopathy.. Confirmed diagnosis: Ocular Tuberculosis. Differential diagnosis includes: Ocular Tuberculosis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Ocular Tuberculosis

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: An eight-year-old girl presented with complaints of difficulty swallowing, blurry vision, and itching in both eyes for the past two years. Laboratory results showed elevated serum cortisol levels. Upon examination at the eye outpatient department, findings included decreased tear meniscus levels and mild superficial punctate keratitis in the superior region of both corneas. The anterior segment examination revealed no other abnormalities.. Confirmed diagnosis: Triple-A Syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes: Triple-A Syndrome.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Triple-A Syndrome

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: An eight-year-old girl presented with complaints of difficulty swallowing, blurry vision, and itching in both eyes for the past two years. Laboratory results showed elevated serum cortisol levels. Upon examination at the eye outpatient department, findings included decreased tear meniscus levels and mild superficial punctate keratitis in the superior region of both corneas. The anterior segment examination revealed no other abnormalities. Schirmer test showed less than 5mm of wetting of filter paper after five minutes. Both eyes revealed optic disc pallor temporally confirmed on SD-OCT.. Confirmed diagnosis: Triple-A Syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes: Triple-A Syndrome.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Triple-A Syndrome

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 24-year-old female reported experiencing headache, palpitations, chest pain, and blurry vision over the past two months. She was also diagnosed with hypertension and received medication from her general physician. During the examination, her vital signs showed a blood pressure of 180/100 mmHg, a heart rate of 104 bpm, and a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute. The patient was alert and well-oriented. Laboratory tests revealed normal levels of haemoglobin, total leukocyte count, liver function, kidney function, and D-dimer.. Confirmed diagnosis: pheochromocytoma. Differential diagnosis includes: pheochromocytoma.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: pheochromocytoma

knowledge_fragments.content: AIP is a severe, rapidly progressive form of IIP. The short-term mortality rate is 50% or more, and there is no proven treatment. It usually affects previously healthy individuals who develop rapidly progressive respiratory failure.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 75-year-old male reported experiencing blurry vision in the left eye for the past 2 weeks. Initial fundoscopic examination revealed intravitreal hemorrhage and uveitis. Visual acuity was measured at 20/60 in the left eye and 20/30 in the right eye. The patient was administered foscarnet due to concerns about an infectious process. Despite this treatment, his symptoms persisted over the following 2 months, and his visual acuity further declined.. Confirmed diagnosis: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. Differential diagnosis includes: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma

knowledge_fragments.content: Cutaneous manifestations are frequent and often early features of both Kawasaki disease (KD) and multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C). Although these conditions differ in epidemiology and triggers, they share overlapping clinical features and immune-mediated pathogenic mechanisms, making early recognition and differential diagnosis challenging. Dermatologic findings are particularly relevant, as they may represent the first clinical clue and precede severe systemic complications.
knowledge_fragments.title: Cutaneous Clues in Kawasaki Disease: Clinical Implications and Differential Diagnosis with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children. > 1. Background

knowledge_fragments.content: A structured, stepwise approach assists clinicians in rapidly triaging acute vision loss and identifying vision-threatening disease. Each step progressively narrows the differential diagnosis and informs the urgency of investigation and referral. This framework (Figure 1) is intended to support initial localization and triage rather than provide a definitive diagnosis. Paediatric causes and chronic/progressive vision loss are outside the scope of this review.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: An eight-year-old girl presented with complaints of difficulty swallowing, blurry vision, and itching in both eyes for the past two years. Laboratory results showed elevated serum cortisol levels. Upon examination at the eye outpatient department, findings included decreased tear meniscus levels and mild superficial punctate keratitis in the superior region of both corneas. The anterior segment examination revealed no other abnormalities.. Confirmed diagnosis: Triple-A Syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes: Triple-A Syndrome.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Triple-A Syndrome

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: An eight-year-old girl presented with complaints of difficulty swallowing, blurry vision, and itching in both eyes for the past two years. Laboratory results showed elevated serum cortisol levels. Upon examination at the eye outpatient department, findings included decreased tear meniscus levels and mild superficial punctate keratitis in the superior region of both corneas. The anterior segment examination revealed no other abnormalities. Schirmer test showed less than 5mm of wetting of filter paper after five minutes. Both eyes revealed optic disc pallor temporally confirmed on SD-OCT.. Confirmed diagnosis: Triple-A Syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes: Triple-A Syndrome.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Triple-A Syndrome

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 24-year-old female reported experiencing headache, palpitations, chest pain, and blurry vision over the past two months. She was also diagnosed with hypertension and received medication from her general physician. During the examination, her vital signs showed a blood pressure of 180/100 mmHg, a heart rate of 104 bpm, and a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute. The patient was alert and well-oriented. Laboratory tests revealed normal levels of haemoglobin, total leukocyte count, liver function, kidney function, and D-dimer.. Confirmed diagnosis: pheochromocytoma. Differential diagnosis includes: pheochromocytoma.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: pheochromocytoma

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 75-year-old male reported experiencing blurry vision in the left eye for the past 2 weeks. Initial fundoscopic examination revealed intravitreal hemorrhage and uveitis. Visual acuity was measured at 20/60 in the left eye and 20/30 in the right eye. The patient was administered foscarnet due to concerns about an infectious process. Despite this treatment, his symptoms persisted over the following 2 months, and his visual acuity further declined.. Confirmed diagnosis: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. Differential diagnosis includes: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.

tree.case_summary:
A 57-year-old man presents to the emergency department with several days of malaise, weakness, and night sweats. Today, he experienced a headache with blurry vision, thus prompting his presentation. The patient has a history of diabetes and is followed closely by an endocrinologist. Otherwise, he has lost 10 pounds over the past month. His temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 122/90 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a thin man but is otherwise unremarkable. His visual acuity is 20/100 in both eyes, though he says that he normally has 20/20 vision. His gait is mildly ataxic as well, but his neurological exam is otherwise nonfocal. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL
Hematocrit: 31%
Leukocyte count: 57,500/mm^3 with 35% blasts
Platelet count: 109,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 4.1 Eq/L
HCO3-: 22 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Calcium: 10.0 mEq/L

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
B. Acute myelogenous leukemia
C. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
D. Chronic myelogenous leukemia
E. Multiple myeloma

excluded_candidates: Diabetes complication: reason ranked lower due to presence of systemic symptoms and leukocytosis with blasts
Infection: reason ranked lower due to lack of clear infectious symptoms and presence of systemic findings
